title: Floater Finder

objects.text: Prostate-biopsy fragment dependence
A CONCH safety experiment for pathologist review
Ashby Hackathon 2026
Measured development results. Clinical usefulness remains unverified.

notes: Floater Finder measures whether a pathology model depends on a small tissue fragment, and whether that evidence supports useful review. We completed a real-data pipeline and controlled stress experiments. We also rejected two review policies when they failed our development targets. This is a safety experiment with explicit failure gates.
source: Development evidence through commit 06c7b77. No held-out test predictions.

title: The specimen-consistency problem

objects.text: Extraneous tissue can create a diagnostic discrepancy
A disease classifier can recognize cancer without establishing that the tissue belongs to the specimen.
The intended action is focused pathologist review. Original tissue and predictions remain intact.

Actual Radboud tiles

notes: Extraneous tissue can create diagnostic discrepancies. A disease classifier can recognize cancer without establishing that it belongs to the specimen. These are actual PANDA tiles with native benign and pattern-four annotations. Neither is a verified natural floater. The intended output is evidence for pathologist review, while preserving the tissue.

title: CONCH and the review question

objects.text: CONCH supplies reusable visual representations
Fixed morphology prompts support an engineering benign/cancer scorer. They do not certify specimen identity.
Disease prediction
What does the sampled tissue resemble?
Review evidence
Which component is unusual and consequential, and what uncertainty remains?

notes: CONCH provides reusable histology representations. Frozen morphology prompts supply our engineering disease scorer. Specimen consistency is a separate task. We therefore examine visual inconsistency, prediction influence and physical context separately. A piece can influence the cancer prediction and still be entirely genuine.

title: Clean benign/cancer baseline

objects.text: Frozen top-5% pooling, calibration only

Accuracy 83.3%
Balanced accuracy 78.1%
Only 5 of 8 benign hosts start correct. New contamination errors must use those five as the denominator.

notes: The clean top-five-percent scorer is correct on twenty of twenty-four calibration slides, with seventy-eight-point-one percent balanced accuracy. It identifies fifteen of sixteen cancer slides, but only five of eight benign slides. Those five originally correct benign hosts define the new-error denominator. The three initial false positives cannot become new contamination errors.

title: S1: a controlled cancer-fragment stress test

objects.text: 32 benign host slides, 21 reused donor slides

192 trials across 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10% doses
Dose = injected tiles / original host tiles, rounded up
Each donor fragment uses unique four-connected saved tiles with ≥10% native cancer annotation per tile.
Synthetic embedding mixtures and translated placement. No assertion of natural floaters or independent patients.

notes: S1 inserts connected, annotated cancer-positive donor features into benign hosts at six doses. We use thirty-two host slides and twenty-one reused donor slides. Dose means donor tiles divided by original host tiles, rounded up. A new error conflicts with the original host label. The mixture truly contains donor cancer, so this does not prove misrecognition of its pixels.

title: Review utility conflicts with reviewer burden

objects.text: Decision-only hypothetical filtering damages 3/20 originally correct clean predictions and flags 1/26 native cancer components.
40 mixtures reuse 8 hosts. Clean alerts measure review burden, not adjudicated natural-contaminant specificity.
Development targets: ≤10% clean slides alerted and ≤0.5 components per slide

notes: The detector comparison reveals a burden tradeoff. Spatial rules hit thirty-two of forty fragments but alert on nineteen of twenty-four clean slides. Decision dependence hits eight fragments and recovers eight induced-error instances, but alerts on four clean slides. Hypothetical filtering damages three of twenty initially correct clean predictions and flags a genuine cancer component.
source: reports/panda_review_selection_v1.json, comparison calibration. 40 correlated positive-dose mixtures, 24 clean slides, 26 evaluable annotated native-cancer components. Filtering is hypothetical only.

title: The combined v1 policy failed its utility gate

objects.text: 0 / 40 fragments detected

No useful candidate among
81 preregistered rules

0/24 alerts has a 95%
Wilson interval of 0–13.8%
The frozen protocol records rejection. Its final-test job remains blocked.

notes: The combined policy misses every calibration fragment. Five mixtures pass its visual criterion, but none also passes influence. Those five mixtures are nested doses from one host. No useful candidate emerges among eighty-one preregistered rules. Zero clean alerts cannot rescue zero recall. We froze the rejection and blocked its final-test job.

Utility: ≥20% fragment recall, ≥25% induced-error recovery. Five visually qualifying mixtures are five nested doses from one calibration host, not five independent hosts. reports/panda_review_v2_results.md.

title: S2: clean grade scorer before contamination

objects.text: Mean pooling selected before S2 outcomes
Primary calibration: low 8/8, high 4/8. Limited high-grade sensitivity remains explicit.
760 trials across four donor conditions. 32 host slides, 37 donor slides. Exact oracle: 760/760.

notes: S2 now tests low-versus-high predictions using pattern-four-or-five donor material and same-grade controls. We chose mean pooling before stress outcomes. Its clean calibration baseline gets all eight low-grade slides correct, but only four of eight high-grade slides. That limited sensitivity remains explicit. All seven hundred sixty trial records pass exact oracle restoration.

title: Detector v2: a separately versioned ranking study

objects.text: Training selects rank threshold and review cap
Visual anomaly and prediction influence become separate rank features. Geometry contributes observed area and isolation.
Native annotation, injection truth and donor identity enter evaluation only. They never enter the blinded review features.
Known calibration outcomes make this iterative development, not independent validation.

notes: Version two tests ranked review instead of requiring every signal to pass a strict conjunction. Training selects thresholds and review caps. Visual, influence and geometry features enter the ranking. Injection truth, donor identity and native annotation remain evaluation-only. Previously seen calibration outcomes make this iterative development, not independent validation.

title: Ranked review still fails useful calibration recall

objects.text: Unbudgeted top-one review flags 14 native cancer components. It exceeds both review-burden targets.
No supported v2 policy and no validated useful improvement over v1. The 24-slide final test remains blocked.

notes: The selected rank detects twenty-two of one hundred twenty training fragments, but zero of forty on known calibration. Its one clean calibration alert contains native cancer. An unbudgeted ranking hits twenty-one fragments but alerts on every clean slide and flags fourteen native cancer components. That exceeds the burden targets. We found no useful validated improvement over version one.

title: What the experiment demonstrates

objects.text: Demonstrated

Verified PANDA-to-CONCH pipeline
S1 synthetic model-sensitivity effects
S2 null primary calibration outcome
Two review policies rejected honestly
Still unverified

Naturally occurring floater detection
Patient-level independence
Clinical cancer or grading validity
Independent final-test performance
Preserving a negative result is part of the safety check.

notes: We demonstrate a verified pipeline, S1 sensitivity, a negative primary S2 result and two rejected review policies. We do not establish natural-floater detection or clinical usefulness. Reused donors, unknown patient overlap and representative sampling limit inference. Artificial edge placement also simplifies geometry. The twenty-four final slides remain unscored.
